newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul blames north for attack on defector.
newsitem.headline: Seoul blames north for attack on defector.

text.p: A North Korean defector to South Korea was shot and injured in an attack near Seoul which a senior police officer said was apparently ordered by the communist north.
The attack came as China agonised over what to do about a high North Korean offical now holed up in the South Korean mission in Beijing and seeking asylum in the south.

The police officer said he suspected North Korean agents carried out Saturday's shooting to send a stark warning to the south over the defection attempt by Hwang Jang-yop, a member of the secretariat of North Korea's ruling Workers Party.

Tensions rose even higher on the divided peninsula after Hwang arrived by taxi at Seoul's Beijing mission last Wednesday. South Korea says he sought asylum in the south, while North Korea insists he was kidnapped.
Analysts in Beijing said China was unlikely to make a decision on the asylum request until after North Korea celebrated the 55th birthday of its top leader, Kim Jong-il, on Sunday.
The police officer identified the man shot near Seoul as Li Il-nam (known in South Korea as Lee Han-yong) and said he was a nephew of a girlfriend of Kim Jong-il.
Li, 36, was shot outside his home at Bundang, just south of the South Korean capital, by two men late on Saturday, he told Reuters.
A nurse at a nearby hospital said he later underwent surgery but she gave no details of his condition.
Hwang's apparent betrayal caused a massive loss of face for a North Korean government already reeling from severe food shortages and economic disasters.
He was ranked 24th in the Stalinist state's hierarchy and would be the most senior Pyongyang official to seek asylum in the South.
The Chinese government has to decide whether to allow him to be flown to Seoul, where he could be expected to reveal crucial secrets about the North Korean state, or to send him back to Pyongyang.
Hwang, the scholarly architect of North Korea's national ideology of Juche, or self-reliance, was reported to be adamant that he wanted to go to South Korea and nowhere else.
"I will die here if my determination to go to South Korea cannot be realised," he said in a statement released by Seoul authorities.

Beijing has appealed for calm while it investigates and South Korea appeared to accept this approach after a meeting between its Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha and Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen in Singapore.
"I think we have started a good discussion with China and we have to wait and see," Yoo said on Saturday. "I don't think that it's right now to make any judgment on this."
Fearing retaliation, even before the shooting near Seoul, South Korea had ordered tighter security at all its overseas missions.

The South Korean police officer said a full-scale manhunt was under way for the presumed North Korean gunmen. Li was the first North Korean defector to be shot in the south since the 1950-53 Korean War ended, he said.
Despite the 1953 truce, the two Koreas have remained implacable foes. Their tense border, bristling with advanced weapons, is today the last Cold War frontier.
